clue.text: Town memorably manufacturing a pie

indicators.note: manufacturing means making something out of raw material, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A town remembered chiefly for turning out a particular pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufacturing' rearranges the letters of TOWN and MEMORABLY. The whole clue doubles as the definition: this Leicestershire town in England is famous for its pork pies, which carry protected regional status.
explanation.definitionFit: The English market town gives its name to a famous raised pork pie, so the town is memorable for producing one.

clue.text: Report written up about independent web business

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed round the other
in a down clue, writing a word upward means its letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: to report a story is to relate it

explanation.surface: A news item, written up, about some independent online company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside RELATE to give RELIATE; 'written up' then reverses it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An online retailer, a shop that trades over the internet, is a business that lives on the web.

clue.text: Set off and attempted to tour the eastern part of Augsburg, Germany

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all round it, so one piece goes around the others

parts.note: attempted means tried

indicators.note: the east of a word written left to right is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone set out and tried to see the eastern side of a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tour' wraps the attempt around the eastern letter of Augsburg and the country's abbreviation; 'the eastern part' means the final letter, not a region of Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger an alarm or an explosion is to set it off, a straightforward synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Dark and almost monstrous at heart

parts.note: nigh means nearly or almost, as in 'nigh on impossible'

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here the fifth of nine

explanation.surface: Something dark and nearly monstrous deep down, like a villain's soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' reads as an adverb on 'monstrous' but supplies NIGH; 'at heart' gives T, the middle letter of MONSTROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkness is the hours after sunset, so the noun 'dark' names that time, as in 'after dark'.

clue.text: Complete plan for banking agreement

parts.note: over means finished or complete, as in 'the game is over'
a draft is an outline plan

explanation.surface: A finished scheme for a deal between banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank arrangement letting a customer spend beyond the account balance, up to an agreed limit.

clue.text: Burn British and foreign currency

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: An instruction to set fire to pounds and overseas money alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To brand livestock is to burn a mark into the hide with a hot iron.

clue.text: Type of film seen in one art gallery

parts.note: an ace is the one in a suit of playing cards
the Tate is the group of national art galleries in London and elsewhere

explanation.surface: A kind of movie being shown in a single gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type of film' looks like a genre of cinema; it is the photographic material, and 'seen in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellulose acetate was the safety base used for photographic and cinema film stock.

clue.text: Actor enters without brother and grandma

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece is wrapped around another

parts.note: to pierce something is to enter it by force
bro is informal for brother
nan is an informal word for grandmother

explanation.surface: A performer comes on stage minus a sibling but with a grandmother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense 'outside', so the word for enters wraps the brother.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish film star is best known for playing James Bond in four films.

clue.text: Two idiots initiating one state shooting, perhaps

indicators.note: initiating means starting off, so these letters come at the front of what follows
two signals the following word is taken twice

parts.note: an ass is a fool
I is the Roman numeral for one
a nation is a state or country

explanation.surface: A pair of fools start a single country's shooting war.
explanation.definitionFit: A political killing may be carried out by gunfire, so a shooting is one example; 'perhaps' flags the example.

clue.text: Rebel army leads intelligence in retreat from Baghdad

indicators.note: leads means goes in front, so this piece comes first

parts.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army, was a rebel paramilitary force

indicators.note: retreating means moving backwards, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: IQ is intelligence quotient, a measure of intelligence

explanation.surface: An insurgent force heads intelligence-gathering while pulling out of the Iraqi capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from Baghdad' is the definition, an adjective phrase meaning belonging to the city's country.
explanation.definitionFit: Baghdad is the capital of Iraq, so someone or something from there is of that nation.

clue.text: They're woolly and are horribly greasy on the outside

definitions.note: a plural phrase: woolly things, matters that are unclear

indicators.note: being on the outside means wrapping round another piece
horribly suggests something badly mangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sheep, perhaps, that are woolly and disgustingly greasy outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges GREASY to GREYAS, which goes 'on the outside' of ARE. 'woolly' suggests fleece but means vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambiguous situations not clearly covered by rules are vague, or woolly, in their boundaries.

clue.text: Hash dealer almost gets sent down

indicators.note: to make a hash of something is to mess it up, so these letters are jumbled
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word gets is dropped

explanation.surface: A cannabis seller nearly ends up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hash' looks like the drug but is the anagram signal on DEALER plus GET; 'sent down' suggests jail but means demoted.
explanation.definitionFit: A football team relegated is moved down a division, so it has been demoted to a lower league.

clue.text: In Japan, no doctor starts to access medical archives

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: In Japan, no doctor may begin to look at medical records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' is not a negative: Noh, also spelt No, is classical Japanese theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Noh is a classical form of Japanese stage theatre, so in Japan it is a kind of play.

clue.text: Crest removed from sweet piece of jewellery

indicators.note: a crest is the top, so the first letter is taken off in this across entry

parts.note: a pear drop is a pear-flavoured boiled sweet, a British confectionery

explanation.surface: A decorative crest taken off a sweet to make a trinket.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendant earring hangs below the lobe, a type of personal ornament.

clue.text: Very severe restrictions and punishments

parts.note: penal can mean extremely severe, as in penal rates of tax
ties are bonds or constraints

explanation.surface: A list of harsh limits and sanctions.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctions imposed for breaking rules or laws, such as fines or free kicks, are synonyms.

clue.text: Musical biopic produced in Australia

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: produced means made

explanation.surface: A film about a composer's life, shot down under.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a location shoot in Australia, but 'in' simply places the word for produced inside the country's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1984 film tells the life of Mozart, so it is a film biography of a composer.

clue.text: Volunteers turning up, here and now

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the letters upward, so in reverse

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve army
present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: Volunteers arrive, here and now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' looks like 'arriving' but reverses TA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means currently, at this moment, a direct equivalent of the adverb.

clue.text: Woman from Kigali managed extra staff

indicators.note: extra as a Latin prefix means outside, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
a wand is a rod or staff

explanation.surface: A woman from an African capital ran an organisation with more employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extra staff' suggests more workers, but 'extra' is the Latin prefix for outside, so managed goes around staff; bloggers found this a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Kigali is the capital of Rwanda, so a woman from there is a native of that country.

clue.text: Examiner in car company faces rising corruption

indicators.note: faces means stands in front of, so this piece comes first

parts.note: Audi is a German car maker

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upward, so in reverse

parts.note: rot is decay or corruption

explanation.surface: An inspector at a car firm confronts growing graft.
explanation.definitionFit: An accountant who inspects a company's books is an examiner of its finances.

clue.text: After excellent glass of beer, finish off a shot?

indicators.note: after says this piece follows the one before it

parts.note: the tops is slang for excellent

indicators.note: finishing something off removes its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a pint is the standard British measure of beer

explanation.surface: Having downed a fine beer, someone wonders about knocking back a quick drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests a drink after the beer but is a stroke in tennis or table tennis; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball hit with forward spin is a kind of stroke in tennis or table tennis.

clue.text: Person used to drink wine very early in the day

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a pawn is someone exploited by others
red is red wine

explanation.surface: A man drinking wine at dawn is being used.
explanation.definitionFit: Before sunrise, the hours just ahead of first light, an adjective for very early morning.

clue.text: Ascetic, dispirited Hindu leaving India

parts.note: dispirited means sad

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so these letters are taken out

explanation.surface: A low-spirited holy man departs from India.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu holy man who renounces worldly life is a religious ascetic.

clue.text: I'm a male with universal, elevated taste

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means raised up, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: U is the British film certificate meaning universal

explanation.surface: A man boasts of his broad, refined palate.
explanation.definitionFit: The savoury fifth basic flavour, alongside sweet, sour, salty and bitter.

clue.text: Men got led out for military occupation

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers were marched out to take up a position.
explanation.definitionFit: A position or foothold seized and held by troops is a lodgment.

clue.text: On account of two people performing together, love ensues!

indicators.note: ensues means follows, so this piece comes after the one before

parts.note: a duet is a piece for two performers
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Because of a singing double act, romance follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means because of, a direct equivalent of the clue's prepositional phrase.

clue.text: Engineer from America rounding St. Lucia and heading for Ecuador

indicators.note: rounding taken loosely as turning about, so these letters are rearranged
heading means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A sailor from the US circles a Caribbean island then sets course for South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounding' rearranges ST LUCIA to CTUALIS, a stretched use as bloggers noted; 'Engineer' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer something is to bring it about, to make real what was only planned.

clue.text: Muse are making a comeback, then cancel tour halfway through

indicators.note: making a comeback means going back, so these letters read in reverse
cancelling the tour cuts it short
halfway through means only the first half survives

explanation.surface: The rock band Muse return, then call off their tour midway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a comeback' reverses ARE to ERA; 'cancel' and 'halfway through' cut TOUR to TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek muse of lyric and love poetry is one of the nine Muses.

clue.text: Film's novel starting point?

definitions.note: the possessive here stands for 'film is', so the definition is a noun phrase naming a film, a fair contraction in cryptic grammar

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: What a movie's book source was: its origin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book the film came from, but it is the anagram signal on STARTING POINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Danny Boyle's 1996 film, adapted from Irvine Welsh's novel, about Edinburgh heroin users.
